Weak points are terminology taste: it coins 「层片」 for stratum, leaves 「\text{relevant}」 untranslated inside the decomposition formula, and uses Taiwan/Japanese-flavored choices 「本征」 (proper) and 「解消」 (resolution), consistent throughout but non-mainland standard.

Fluent and mathematically accurate, and its crepant rendering 「保持典范类的奇点消解」 is thoughtful. However the clause 「满足 Verdier 对偶性。」 is displaced into the following \begin{defn} environment, so it typesets inside the definition box; the displayed line 「\ab(\text{维数为 } 4)」 drops the word summand/直和项 entirely; and hard Lefschetz is misrendered as 「强 Lefschetz 定理」, with 「层」 overloaded for both sheaf and stratum (「相关层」).

Accurate with the best standard terminology of the set (「真态射」 for proper, 「W-主齐性空间」 for torsor, 「硬莱夫谢茨定理」), and structure is preserved exactly. But two displayed text fragments are left untranslated: 「\ab(\text{a summand of dimension } 4)」 and 「\bigoplus_{Y_\lambda\text{ relevant}}」; and a few constructions are stiff, e.g. 「若对所有层 Y_λ 变化」 and 「曲面上的点集的希尔伯特概形」.

Very accurate and the most natural Chinese of the set (「反常层并非层，而是集中在次数 [−dim Y, 0] 的复形」), with proper correctly 「真（proper）态射」. But it leaves the same two displayed fragments in English (「a summand of dimension 4」, 「relevant」) and coins nonstandard terms: 「泛有限」 for generically finite and 「W-扭」 for torsor.

Complete and accurate, and alone among the top group it translates every displayed text fragment (「\text{相关}」 and 「\ab(\text{一个 } 4 \text{ 维的直和项})」). Terminology is the weak spot: torsor becomes the coined 「W-旋子」, and proper is consistently rendered 「紧合(映射/态射)」, a complex-analytic/Taiwan flavor rather than the AG-standard 真态射/固有态射; everything else (可构造层, 反常层, 支撑条件, 硬 Lefschetz) is standard.

Reads smoothly and omits nothing, with deliberate English glosses, but the central hypothesis term proper is systematically mistranslated as 「完备(映射/态射)」 — a complete morphism is a genuinely different notion — and hard Lefschetz becomes 「强 Lefschetz 定理」. Its gloss for crepant, 「同调平凡解消」, is wrong (crepant ≠ homologically trivial), it abbreviates constructible to the nonstandard 「可构层」, adds 「不妨取」 where the source says 'Then for', and rewrites K\"unneth as literal Künneth, which breaks pdfLaTeX.

Math displays, environments and citations are all preserved and the display texts are translated (「\text{相关}」, 「一个维数为 4 的直和项」), but 「存在奇异的 crepant 解消」 mistranslates 'crepant resolution of singularities' — it now asserts the resolution itself is singular. It also abbreviates 相交同调/相交复形 to the nonstandard 「交同调」/「交复形」, leaves the theorem names (K\"unneth formula, Leray/Serre spectral sequence) in English, and mixes languages mid-sentence with 「若唯一的 relevant 分层」.

Fully complete: all 11 subsections, every environment, all 114 display equations, labels, cites and both figures match the source, and no mathematical claim is altered (string/dilaton/WDVV equations, localization formulas all identical). Terminology is mostly sound but nonstandard in places: 'proper morphism' becomes '本征态射' and 'proper DM stack' becomes '本征的 Deligne–Mumford 栈' (真/紧合 is standard), and the dilaton equation is '胀子方程'. One awkward phrase: '我们切去不平衡的部分，即着为蓝色的部分' ('即着' is garbled for '着色为蓝色').

Complete and exact on structure and all 114 display equations; it even wraps two wide align blocks in {\small}, a harmless improvement. It uses the most consistently standard terminology of the seven (固有态射, 伸缩子方程, 惯性叠, 轨形, 推前) and reads very naturally. The one clear accuracy slip is 'a unique rational curve' rendered as '一条孤立的有理曲线' ('isolated' for 'unique'). '取值映射' for evaluation maps is unusual (赋值/求值映射 standard), and the added '其中目标为 X' is a small redundant insertion.

Complete, with all math, labels, cites and figures preserved verbatim, and the prose is accurate ('真态射' correctly distinguishes proper from '完美' perfect). Terminology is patchy: pluri-Hodge becomes '多霍奇层' (多重 Hodge usual), it alternates between '轨形' and untranslated 'orbifold' ('orbifold Riemann-Roch 定理'), and between '三维簇' and '三维流形' for threefold. Small shifts of nuance such as '粗略地' for 'Naively' and untranslated names ('Lee--Qu', 'Milanov') alongside 周祐正.

Complete and accurate in content, with math, labels and figures intact. Consistency is the problem: inertia stack is '惯性叠' once (correct) but '惰性叠' elsewhere ('我们将研究惰性叠（inertia stack）'), pushforward is both '推前' and '前推', and Riemann–Roch is translated '黎曼--罗赫' in one subsection but left untranslated elsewhere. The opening quotes are ASCII straight quotes ('"计数"'), which will not typeset as proper opening quotes in LaTeX.

Complete and very accurate: every equation, label, cite and figure matches, and terminology is clean and standard (紧合态射, 伸缩子方程, 惯性叠, 轨形, 前推, 完美障碍理论). Minor blemishes: 'threefold' is rendered '三维流形' (三维簇 is safer for a variety), and spacing around math is dropped in the first half ('设\(X\)是光滑射影簇') but kept later ('设 \(s \in \Z\)'), an inconsistency rather than an error. Fluency is otherwise excellent and punctuation is consistent.

The most fluent prose of the seven, accurate, with helpful English glosses ('胀子方程（dilaton equation）'). Its systematic flaw is terminology: both 'perfect' and 'proper' become '完备' ('完备复形', '沿完备态射的前推', '完备 DM 叠'), conflating two distinct hypotheses (the gloss 'perfect morphism' partly saves it); '重覆盖' for multiple cover and '多倍 Hodge' for pluri-Hodge are also nonstandard. It also deletes the ~250 commented-out lines of the duplicate figure present in the source — no effect on the typeset output, but the source text is not fully preserved.

Structurally complete and mathematically faithful — all environments, equations, labels and figures present and unchanged (including the commented-out figure block). However the Chinese prose is set with half-width ASCII commas throughout (129 instances, e.g. '其中 \(C\) 是某个 Calabi-Yau 三维流形中唯一的一条有理曲线,其法丛为'), which typesets with inconsistent punctuation. Terminology is weak in spots: '完全复形/完全态射' for perfect, '\(\mu_2\)-丛胚' for gerbe, '膨胀方程' for dilaton equation, and the heading '公理性性质'; 'gravitational descendants' is mistranslated as '引力下降部分'.

Faithful and complete: all 57 display blocks, environments, labels and cites are preserved byte-identically. Terminology is consistent and mostly standard (墙交叉, 胀子方程, 万有曲线, 完美障碍理论), though 'proper' is rendered 本征 and the annotation in the F_{\star,d} display ('fixed and (v=0) is not a common zero') is left in English. The Chinese reads naturally, with only small slips such as 直接行到自身. No mathematical claims were altered.

Accurate, complete and very readable; 'proper'→固有 is standard, but wall-crossing as 过墙 and 'toy example' as 简化例子 are idiosyncratic. Two added {\small} wrappers around long displays modify the source LaTeX, and a couple of sentences leave a lone '。' on the line after a display (e.g. after \int_{\P^{n-1}} H^{n-1} = 1). No mathematical errors found.

Complete and largely correct, but visibly more translationese: 不动点轨迹由一族图来指标化, 我们需要求 (for 'we need to require'), and the calque 回忆 Hassett's 的加权带点曲线模空间. The example titles [Second toy example]/[Another toy example] and the F_{\star,d} formula annotation stay in English, and terminology drifts (真（proper）, 膨胀子方程, 越墙). Math, labels and environments are all intact.

Accurate and complete with exact LaTeX preservation (even \text{\'et} kept). The main weaknesses are terminology choices: 泛曲线 (universal curve), 镜像变换 (mirror map), 膨胀子方程 (dilaton), 真（proper）, 越墙 for wall-crossing, plus the leftover calque Hassett\textquotesingle s 加权模空间 and a lone '。' after two displays. Otherwise smooth academic Chinese with no changed mathematical claims.

The most natural Chinese of the set; all content is present and the math is untouched. Terminology is a personal but consistent system: 壁穿越/腔 for wall-crossing/chamber, 紧合 for proper, C^{\times}-旋子 for torsor, 五次三维流形 and Grassmann 流形 (varieties as 流形), and 带权点曲线 for weighted pointed curve. No mistranslations of substance were found.

Fluent and helpfully glossed (前稳定拟映射（prestable quasimap）), with everything present, but several slips: 'it will travel directly to itself along the C^{\times}-action' becomes 它在 \(\C^{\times}\) 作用下保持不动, 'proper' and 'perfect' are both rendered 完备 (完备 DM 叠 / 完备障碍理论), an unannounced addition （即结点和标记点） explains 'special points', and the diagram label \text{\'et} is rewritten as \text{平展}, changing the output; 泛曲线 for universal curve is also nonstandard.

All content, formulas and environments survive, and the meaning is rarely distorted, but the polish is weak. Half-width commas and parentheses are used throughout the Chinese text (本讲中的主要穿墙定理与主空间构造来自...), 其光滑 is ungrammatical, 'quintic threefold' is consistently reduced to 五次超曲面, and 'node smoothing' becomes 节点磨光参数; 泛曲线 and 穿墙 are nonstandard. Lone '。' lines after displays recur.

Faithful throughout, with every environment, figure, footnote, label and formula preserved and the long displayed identities reproduced exactly. Terminology is internally consistent but follows a Taiwan-school register that deviates from mainland standard usage: 栈 for stack, 本征 for proper, 环簇/环扇 for toric variety/fan, and an odd 单位扇形 for the unit sector. Minor inconsistencies remain in cite optional arguments: “定理~1.16--1.17” is localized but “Conjecture~1.6” is left in English.

Very faithful and fluent, with mainland-standard terminology (叠, 固有, 丰沛, 临界点集, 单位扇区) used consistently. Small blemishes: an added \enlargethispage{3pt} not in the source, the addition “没有额外对数结构” (extra word 额外), “被 e_max 一致控制” for “uniformly bounded”, and the final corollary's “当 (X, V) 时，上述猜想…” slightly misses “The above conjecture for (X, V)”. Conifold gap becomes “锥形奇点间隙条件”, inserting 奇点.

Complete and mathematically faithful, with structure, labels and all displayed formulas intact. However “proper” is rendered 真, producing confusing sentences such as “非常好，但它不是真的” and “是真且对数光滑的”; other weak choices include 扭的 for twisted, 边长度 for edge length, and translationese like “它在预期的余维数上定义了一个光滑的零截面”. Terms like R-spin and conifold gap are left in English, which is defensible.

Careful and accurate, helpfully glossing key terms in parentheses (装饰热带型, 一致极大退化, 真（proper）的). The same 真-for-proper choice yields awkward phrasing (“它不是真的”), and twisted is compressed to 扭; Lefschetz is rendered 莱夫谢茨. All math, labels, cites and both tikz figures are exactly preserved, and cite optional arguments are consistently kept in English.

Fluent, natural Chinese with mainland-standard terms (叠, 紧合, 丰沛, 紧型) and fully consistent localization of cite optional arguments (定理/猜想). The notable terminology slip is rendering threefold/fourfold as 流形: “Calabi-Yau 三维流形” and “Fano 四维流形” should be 三维簇/四维簇 for varieties; the source's “zero section” also becomes 零点集, a reasonable but free reading. Everything else, including both figures and every displayed formula, is preserved.

Complete and accurate, and unusually diligent in glossing technical terms with English (穿孔（punctured）, 接触阶（contact orders）, 装饰热带型, 平衡条件). But its core term choices are nonstandard: proper is rendered 专有 throughout (“它不是专有的”, “专有 DM 叠” — should be 紧合/固有), ample becomes 充裕 (“充裕线丛”, “V 是充裕的”), and the conifold gap condition becomes “锥流形间隙条件”. Prestable is rendered 前稳定 rather than the usual 预稳定.

Mathematically faithful and structurally complete, but the prose is marred by pervasive half-width ASCII punctuation (112 ',' and zero full-width '，', plus half-width parentheses and '?') where all other translations use proper Chinese punctuation, and by orphan punctuation lines after display math (“。现在，一个 R-映射…” and “,其中”). Small accuracy slips: “在期望余维数处定义/光滑” misreads “of the expected codimension”, and “五次超曲面” drops “threefold”. Terminology is off in places: “超级势” for superpotential, “虚循环” for virtual cycle, and “三维流形/四维流形” for threefold/fourfold.

Faithful throughout; 'generically semisimple' is correctly rendered as '使量子乘积在一般点处半单', and author names are properly identified (刘治宇–阮勇斌, 张怀良–郭帅–李骏). All environments, labels, cites, both tikz figures, the BPS table and every formula are present and byte-identical apart from translated \text{...}. Only quibbles: the coinage '锥形点' for conifold point and '墙交叉' for wall-crossing are less standard than keeping 'conifold 点'/'穿墙'.

Accurate and complete, with good standard terms ('锥形奇点', '过墙', '间隙' for gap). However B silently rewrites source typography: hyphens become en-dashes everywhere ('Calabi--Yau', 'Gromov--Witten', 'Picard--Fuchs'), the X_{3,3} align* is re-broken across lines, and the display '引入 \(D_u = ...\) 及生成元' is split into a \begin{gathered} block — layout changes, though compilable. '虚圈' for virtual cycle and the clipped subject-dropping style ('考虑…，问…') slightly reduce polish; '在一般点半单' is correct.

Complete with zero math deviations (all formulas, table entries and figures byte-identical), and nice touches like '锥形点（conifold）' glosses. But terminology is inconsistent: 'Gromov-Witten' is kept in English early on, then becomes '格罗莫夫–威滕不变量' from section 四种理论 onward. '使量子积一般半单' mistranslates 'generically semisimple', and phrasings like '二部图和' (for bipartite graph sum) and '右端的两个对应 \Mbar_g 的两个边界层' are awkward.

Complete and mathematically faithful; the conifold discussion is handled well ('锥点缝隙（conifold gap）条件'). Terminology is uneven: 'leading BPS invariants' becomes '主要 BPS 不变量' (should be 领头/前几个), and Gromov-Witten is transliterated as '格罗莫夫–威滕' while the section title keeps 'GW' — even mixing within one line of the footnote ('五次格罗莫夫--Witten 理论'). Several '~\Cref' ties are dropped ('我们看到 \Cref{tab:quinticbps} 的每一列'), risking bad line breaks.

Very accurate and complete; every environment, footnote and number is present, and tricky passages like 'the individual twisted graph contributions involve extra generators' come out right ('则单个扭曲图的贡献会涉及额外的生成元'). E systematically drops the final period inside display math (~9 places, e.g. '\(h_{\alpha} = \zeta_5^{\alpha}\lambda\)' without '.'), a consistent but non-source punctuation style, and attaches inline math directly to CJK characters without spaces. '多重覆叠变换' for multicover is slightly off ('多重覆盖' is usual).

The most fluent academic prose of the set, with helpful bilingual glosses ('多重覆盖变换（multicover transformation）', '锥流形间隙（conifold gap）') and clean LaTeX exactly mirroring the source. Two coinages are unusual: '锥流形点' for conifold point (used throughout the crucial boundary-conditions section) and '原生不变量' for primary invariants. '在一般意义下半单' again blurs 'generically semisimple'.

Content is complete and the math is intact, but terminology is the weakest here: orbifold is mistranslated as '轨道点' / '轨道正则性' (standard is 轨形), 'holomorphic ambiguity' becomes '全纯含糊性', and virtual cycle becomes '虚基本类'. Internal inconsistency abounds: the table caption says '五次三维流形' while the text says '五次超曲面', and author names flip between '郭帅' (title) and 'Guo--Janda--Ruan'. There is also a typo ('带理后代插入' for 带有理后代插入) and periods dropped from several display equations.

Faithful and complete with all math, labels and environments exact, but 'toric' is systematically rendered as 环 (e.g. "非紧的环 Calabi--Yau 三维簇", "环图由两个三角形组成"), which reads as 'ring' rather than toric. The hypothesis 'the moduli space is not proper' is mistranslated as "模空间...不是本征的" (本征 means 'eigen'), and the resolved conifold becomes the idiosyncratic "已解消的锥形点". Otherwise the prose is accurate and reads well.

A reliable, concise translation with no changed mathematical claims; 'not proper' is acceptably rendered as "模空间...不固有". Its main weakness is terminology: the recurring 'ansatz' is translated as "表达式猜想" instead of the standard 拟设, and Lefschetz thimble becomes "Lefschetz 膜". Fluency is good, with natural subject-dropping academic Chinese ("考虑总空间", "选取标架").

Complete and mostly accurate, but 'the moduli space is not proper' is mistranslated as "模空间 \Mbar_{g,0}(X_p,d) 不是真的" ('is not genuine'), which loses the properness hypothesis. 'Pairing' is twice garbled to "配为" (for 配对为), and the invariants ω_{g,n} are called "数量". It sensibly keeps 'remodeling 猜想' and 'Lefschetz thimble' in English; otherwise readable.

Accurate and fluent with careful details ("我们的约定相差一个因子"), but it transliterates Gromov-Witten as "格罗莫夫–威滕理论" throughout, inconsistent with the 'GW 理论' of its own section title, and keeps 'framing' in Latin script ("我们取 framing f \in \Z"). 'Not proper' becomes the odd "不是真（proper）的", thimble becomes the nonstandard "Lefschetz 鞘", and a stray \bigskip is added at the end.

The strongest translation: correct properness ("模空间...不是紧合的"), standard choices throughout (标架, 消解锥形奇点（resolved conifold）, 双标度极限, Lefschetz 顶针, 拟设), and very natural academic Chinese. Only minor slips: 'threefold' as "三维流形", the awkward "有趣的是点 q → 1/p²", and rescaling rendered as "对特征标作伸缩". All math, labels and environments are exact.

Very fluent and professional, helpfully glossing key terms in English ("标架（framing）", "带框 R-矩阵（framed R-matrix）", "Lefschetz 顶针（Lefschetz thimbles）"). Its one real error is 'is not proper' mistranslated as "模空间...不是专有的" (proprietary); 'generically distinct' is also softened to "在一般意义下互不相同" and 'characters' becomes 特征标群. Everything else, including all hypotheses and formulas, is faithfully preserved.

Complete and largely faithful, but several standard terms are wrong or nonstandard: the toric fan becomes "X_p 的扇形的一维锥" (扇形 = sector), 'preserves the Calabi-Yau form' becomes "其作用保持 Calabi-Yau 型" (changing 'form' to 'type'), and 'intersection numbers' is rendered "交数". 'Threefold' again becomes 三维流形, and the PDF-bookmark argument of texorpdfstring is left in English. Properness ("不是固有的") is, however, handled acceptably.

Faithful to the source structure: the parenthetical correctly scopes figure insertion to talks besides the author's and Guo's ("除我本人与郭帅的报告之外的所有报告; 其中部分图是事后用 Codex 或 Claude Code 插入的"). Main weakness is punctuation: it uses half-width commas and semicolons with spaces (", " and "; ") instead of full-width Chinese punctuation throughout, plus a stray space in "温耀雄 指出". Rendering "errors in my lectures" as "我的讲义中的任何错误" slightly shifts lectures to lecture notes, and keeping "log GLSM" in English is acceptable but inconsistent with the 对数 GLSM choice elsewhere.

Very fluent, well-punctuated academic Chinese ("谨致歉意", "实验性转录"). However it restructures the first sentence into "除我本人的报告和郭帅的报告外，笔记均为现场用 TeX 记录", which turns the English parenthetical (all notes are live-TeXed; figures for talks besides mine and Guo's were inserted later) into a claim that the live-TeXing itself excludes those talks — a small but real shift in meaning. Everything else is accurate and complete.

Essentially publishable as is. Keeps the English sentence structure faithfully ("暑期学校讲座的现场 \TeX{} 笔记（除我本人以及郭帅的讲座外，部分插图是事后用 Codex 或 Claude Code 插入的）"), renders "experimental AI-generated transcriptions" cleanly as "\textbf{实验性} AI 转录稿", uses consistent full-width punctuation and natural academic register ("我深表歉意", "请告知我"). Every sentence of the source is present with no additions or omissions.

Accurate and complete with natural phrasing ("在此一并致歉", "敬请告知") and correct scoping of the figure-insertion parenthetical. Minor nits: "现场 TeX 速记稿" uses 速记 (stenography) for live-TeXing, and "均以中文给出" is slightly stiffer than 进行/讲授 for "were given in Chinese". Full-width punctuation and LaTeX are clean.

Content is accurate and complete, but the register is noticeably colloquial for an academic abstract: "用中文讲的", "补上的", "请告诉我", "除我自己". "试验性" is a less standard choice than 实验性 for "experimental" here, and "\textbf{试验性}地由 AI 生成" awkwardly splits the bolded adjective from the verb. LaTeX and \textbf are intact.

Fluent prose, but several small meaning shifts: "课程" (courses) is used for the summer school talks/lectures throughout, "errors in my lectures" is softened to "我本人讲义中的疏漏" (oversights in my lecture notes), and "all of my other notes" becomes "我以往所有的笔记" (all my past notes). Like B, it restructures the parenthetical to claim the live recording itself excludes the author's and Guo's talks ("除我本人及郭帅的课程外均为现场录入").

Accurate and complete with standard terminology ("实验性", "对数 GLSM"). Minor issues: "会后" (after the conference) slightly over-specifies "later"; "现场 TeX 记录笔记" is redundant (记录 + 笔记); the register dips into the colloquial ("用中文讲的", "请告诉我"); and there is a stray space in "感谢 周祐正". Overall a solid, readable translation.

Complete and mathematically faithful, with all environments and formulas retained. The consistent use of “栈” and “广群” is less aligned with the expected “叠/群胚” terminology, and leaving “is a vector bundle on” and “isomorphism classes in” inside formulas makes the Chinese feel unfinished.

Very complete and generally fluent; “半稳定部分” and “由整体截面生成” are clear renderings. However, “局部有限表示” is a poor choice for locally of finite presentation, the added “对某个充分大的整数” is redundant, and the slope-definition wording around “上述不等式（其中子层记为” is awkward; the tabular preamble was also altered.

Mathematically faithful and complete, but the Chinese has avoidable editing slips such as “一族族的同构类” and “或等价地等价于”. “无环的” for acyclic is nonstandard (零调 is expected), and untranslated fragments such as “Slope stability” and “isomorphism classes in” further reduce polish.

The translation is complete and mostly accurate, but “推出函子” for the pushforward q_* is the wrong term (it suggests pushout rather than 前推/推前). Other polish problems include “精细模空间”, “局部有限表示”, and “次数上有界”, while the atlas parenthetical can be read as calling the morphism, rather than U, the atlas.

Excellent, complete rendering with equations and environments intact and consistently readable academic Chinese; “紧合” for proper and “零调” for acyclic are used correctly. Only small terminology choices such as “精细模空间” instead of the more standard “细模空间”, plus occasional English like “Cartesian 图表”, keep it from being publication-ready.

Complete and largely faithful, but repeated “完备复形” for perfect complex is a substantive terminology error, and “完备（proper）” also confuses properness with completeness. Phrases such as “所可表” and “容有泛族” are awkward, and the many parenthetical English glosses make the text less fluent despite intact mathematics.

All environments are present, but the footnote's “大致上是有限表现的” drops “locally” from “locally of finite presentation”. The text also contains “带有所左 G-作用” and “每条线丛”, repeatedly uses the less standard “过滤” for filtration, and changes headings to lowercase θ with new texorpdfstring macros.

Sentence-by-sentence faithful; every tricky passage (log smooth lifting definition, Kato's criterion, the puncturing α(s)=0 argument) is rendered exactly. Main flaws: three \text{...} fragments inside display math are left in English (e.g. "\text{ if there exists } s \in P \text{ such that }" at line 21), and "ghost sheaf" is coined as 「鬼层」 rather than the standard 幽灵层. A few stiff spots like 「对数结构之栈」 (栈 instead of 叠) and 「层片」 for strata.

Faithful and complete, with genuinely fluent restructuring (e.g. 「直观上可把对数光滑性理解为相对于底空间局部具有环面几何的形态」). Terminology control is weaker: 「伴随对数结构」 for "associated log structure" (伴随 normally means adjoint; 相伴 is standard), 「图」 is used for both chart and diagram causing collisions, and "étale"/"Cartesian" are left untranslated throughout (「小 étale 景」, 「Cartesian 图」). Small benign additions like 模叠 for "moduli" at line 305.

Mostly good, but has concrete defects: line 317 renders "a log smooth integral map" as 「对数光滑的对数积（integral）映射」 — the nonsense coinage 对数积 for integral, inconsistent with the translator's own 整的 elsewhere; line 308 inserts 「典范」 (canonical) where the source deliberately says only "log structures"; and "generalization maps" becomes 「广义化映射」 (wrong AG term; the correct pair 特殊化/一般化 is broken). Also inconsistent: 精细的 vs bare "fine" (lines 552, 577), n点 vs n-标记.

Mathematically faithful with flawless LaTeX, but terminology is the worst after G: "integral" is systematically coined as 「对数积」 (reads as "logarithmic product"; lines 23, 27, 33, 140), then the convention flips mid-document to bare English (「是 integral 的」 line 256, 「integral 映射」 line 319), and "fine"/"saturated" similarly switch between 精细/饱和 and bare English. 「图表」 is used for both chart and commutative diagram, a real ambiguity. Fixable by find-replace, but confusing as printed.

The cleanest translation: no mistranslations found anywhere, all \text{...} fragments inside math properly translated (e.g. 「\text{ 若 } n = 0」), fluent natural academic Chinese (「粗略地说，可以把对数光滑理解为相对于底空间局部地是环面的」). Only real blemish: 一般点 is used for both "generic point" and "general point", so line 386's "a generic point or a general smooth point" becomes the ambiguous 「在一般点或一个一般的光滑点η处」; "fs" is left in English after 精细饱和 is introduced.

Strong and consistent (整的/细的/幽灵层/图卡 throughout, helpful English glosses on first use), but marred by a glaring typo at line 75 — a Japanese hiragana の instead of 的: 「它是如下图表の上极限」. Two small unfaithful additions: 「特化映射（或泛化映射）」 at line 388 where the source says only "the specialization map", and 模叠 for "moduli" at line 305. A few clumsy phrases (「纤维化于群胚的范畴」, doubled 「表示为…的表示」 at line 409).

Complete and otherwise decent, but "fine" is systematically mistranslated as 「有限的」 (= finite) in ~15 places, which falsifies statements: 「推出未必是有限的」 for "Pushouts may not be fine" (line 258) is mathematically wrong as printed, and the definition at line 33 becomes self-contradictory (「有限的（fine），若 P 是有限生成的且是整的」). Kato's criterion is garbled by word order: 「的核与余核的挠部分的阶是在 X 上可逆的有限群」 says the orders are finite groups (line 166). "étale" is never translated (「小 'etale site」).

Complete and faithful: all math, figures, labels and the three footnotes preserved verbatim, and subtle claims like "恰好沿 \(zL \subset L\) 与 \(\mc{L}\) 相切" and "沿负实轴 \(z \to 0^-\) 的渐近展开" are rendered exactly. Main weakness is terminology: "tautological" is left in English twice ("稳定图的例子及其相伴的 tautological 类"), "nef" is untranslated, and "KdV hierarchy" becomes "KdV 族". Minor translationese: "work over the Novikov ring" rendered as "在 Novikov 环上展开" and "打开等变参数".

A very strong, complete translation with no detected content errors; tricky sentences such as the Givental 1996 theorem ("它在沿负实轴令 \(z \to 0^-\) 时的渐近展开，等于 I 函数在 \(X\) 上某个 T 不动点处的限制") are exact, and the prose reads like native academic Chinese ("为节约时间并简化记号"). Deductions are terminological: "Lefschetz thimble" is wrongly rendered "Lefschetz 膜" (膜 = membrane; should be 顶针), "étale" is left in French, and "gamma 函数" is left in lowercase Latin. LaTeX is clean, with only in-math \text{} content legitimately translated.

Complete and LaTeX-clean, but with several genuine errors: "up to various prefactors" becomes "在各种前因子范围内" and the whole Givental 1996 sentence is nearly unparsable ("与对应于 \(X\) 上相应于临界点…的 T-不动点的 I-函数在限制后一致"); the footnote "we expand" is mistranslated as "我展开"; "proper" becomes "是真的" (reads as "is true"); "Lefschetz thimble" becomes the nonstandard "喉管". Terminology is also inconsistent: "Gromov-Witten" is Latin in most places but suddenly "格罗莫夫-威滕" later, and "Frobenius 流形" alternates with "弗罗贝尼乌斯流形". Still usable with editing.

Solid and complete, with most hunted items correct ("数值有效（nef）", "平坦单位", "半单", the z→0⁻ asymptotics sentence). Real slips: "Lefschetz thimble" mistranslated as "Lefschetz 闭链" (闭链 = cycle; should be 顶针), "the MSP group" becomes "MSP 群" (reads as a mathematical group), and "using the fact that J solves the quantum connection" is garbled into "利用 \(J\) 求解量子联络这一事实". Terminology is inconsistent across the document: "欧拉向量场" vs "Euler 向量场", "霍奇丛" vs "Hodge 丛", "量子黎曼–罗赫定理" vs "量子 Riemann-Roch 定理".

High quality with the best terminology of the set: "紧合" for proper, "平展覆叠" for étale cover, "Lefschetz 顶针", "扇序列", consistent "伸缩子" for dilaton, and all display math character-identical to the source. The one real error: "symplectic formalism" is rendered "辛形式" (line 414), which collides with the correct use of 辛形式 for "symplectic form" elsewhere and momentarily confuses the section's topic. Minor nits: "KdV 族" for hierarchy, inconsistent spacing around "I 函数/J 函数", and en-dash inconsistencies ("Gromov--Witten" vs "Gromov-Witten").

Careful and complete, but with a real terminology/accuracy error its peers mostly avoided: "proper" is rendered "是完备的" (完备 = complete) at line 25. Other issues: "KdV hierarchy" becomes the nonstandard "KdV 谱系", and "tautological" is rendered "典范类/典范关系", colliding with 典范坐标 for "canonical coordinates" in the same text; "interesting map" is upgraded to "重要的映射". LaTeX shows punctuation drift inside about ten display equations (periods/commas added or removed within the math) and the Chang-Guo-Li theorem header is rewritten with inserted Chinese given names; all formulas themselves remain identical.

Near-publishable: complete, faithful, and the cleanest LaTeX of the set — it is the only translation that keeps the optional theorem argument "[Chang-Guo-Li {\cite[Theorem~2.7]{CGL2026}}]" intact instead of guessing Chinese author names, and all math lines are pairwise identical apart from appropriate \text{} localizations ("\text{遗忘映射}", "\text{偶}/\text{奇}"). Terminology is standard and consistent (叠, 重言, 后代/祖先, 膨胀子, 固有的 for proper), with only "Lefschetz thimble" and "gamma 函数" left in Latin. Fluency is natural; the few quibbles are literalisms like "打开等变参数" and "不接收尾部贡献".

Complete and highly faithful, with every environment and formula retained and the last decomposition correctly rendering ‘a summand’ as ‘直和项’. The Chinese is generally natural; minor untranslated terms such as ‘W-torsor’ and ‘relevant’, plus literal phrasing like ‘在到达那里之前’, prevent a perfect score.

It is usually fluent and faithful, with strong terminology such as ‘保持典范类的奇点消解’ and ‘W 扭子’. However, ‘满足 Verdier 对偶性’ is placed inside the perverse-sheaf definition environment, and the final align reduces ‘a summand of dimension 4’ to the incomplete ‘维数为 4’; these are substantive structural and mathematical wording errors.

Very accurate and complete, and ‘W-主齐性空间’ is a precise rendering of torsor. Polish is uneven: ‘核心’ is nonstandard for the heart of a t-structure, ‘由于 f 是真的’ is awkward, and ‘a summand of dimension 4’ remains in English in the last formula.

The environments and formulas are intact and the prose is mostly clear, but ‘确定’ is stronger than the source’s ‘detect’, and terms such as ‘泛有限’ and ‘W-扭’ are nonstandard for generically finite and torsor. The phrase ‘a summand of dimension 4’ also remains untranslated in the final formula.

All content is present and most prose is faithful, but central terminology is weaker: ‘紧合态射’ is a nonstandard choice for proper morphism and ‘W-旋子’ incorrectly renders torsor. The display defining the Verdier duality functor also drops the source’s final period, a minor mathematical-typesetting and punctuation slip.

Although complete, it repeatedly translates proper as ‘完备’ (including ‘由于 f 是完备的’), thereby changing the central hypothesis, and renders crepant resolution as ‘同调平凡解消’, which asserts a different property. ‘可构层’ is nonstandard for constructible sheaf, and phrasing such as ‘使得对所有 λ 限制 …’ is awkward.

Mostly complete and readable, but ‘存在奇异的 crepant 解消’ says that the resolution itself is singular rather than that it resolves singularities. Terminology is uneven, including ‘交同调/交复形’ for intersection homology/complex and ‘W-主丛’ for torsor; ‘relevant’ is also left untranslated in the smallness definition.

Faithful and complete throughout: every environment, footnote, display and the commented-out figure block are present with formulas identical to the source. The main recurring flaw is rendering pushforward as 推出 ("我们可以把等变 Euler 特征定义为推出"), which standardly means pushout, plus 陈特征标 for Chern character. Prose is natural academic Chinese; minor LaTeX regressions are the systematic use of Unicode en-dashes ("Hirzebruch–Riemann–Roch") instead of -- and an occasional missing sentence period after a display.

Complete and often the most idiomatic of the seven (best terminology in the axiomatic/equivariant slices: 伸缩子方程, 拉格朗日锥, 推前, Euler 示性数). However it changes a mathematical claim: "a unique rational curve" becomes "一条孤立的有理曲线", and "hyperelliptic locus" is mistranslated as 超椭圆部分. LaTeX hygiene is sloppy: orphaned "。" on their own lines after displays, {\small} wrappers added around two align* blocks not in the source, and dropped connector hyphens ("T 等变向量丛").

Accurate and complete in all five slices, with clean structure and full-width punctuation. Terminology is its weak point: it coins 多霍奇 for pluri-Hodge, leaves "orbifold" untranslated ("orbifold 陈特征标", "orbifold Riemann-Roch 定理"), and inconsistently leaves fake/stem in English in the adelic propositions while translating arm/leg/tail. A couple of stiff or grammatically broken spots, e.g. the bare verb in "并用 ω_π^s 扭" and the unfinished "我们令多重覆盖公式" before a display.

Generally faithful and very readable, but with several identifiable defects: 惰性叠 for inertia stack (惰性 = inert), 托德类 for Todd class, and "这并不是正确的配对" dropping the hedging "quite" from "not quite the right pairing". It reorders two display pairs in the quantum-K-of-a-point subsection (the L^{1/2} expansion vs. the ∂^n∘f property, and Lee's correlator formula vs. its expansion) and drops commas inside displays. LaTeX bugs include ASCII straight quotes ("计数", "超大") that typeset wrongly and punctuation stranded on its own lines.

The most consistent translation overall: accurate in every slice (it is the only one to fully render "轨形陈特征和轨形 Todd 类"), complete including the commented-out figure block, and formulas are byte-identical to the source. Its quirks are stylistic rather than wrong: the rare but consistent 紧合态射 for proper morphism, 圈空间 for loop space, 后代 GW 不变量 for descendant, and a no-space style between Chinese and inline math. Fluency is high, with good sentence restructuring ("由 Serre 对偶可知", "然后计算前推即可").

Contains the most serious accuracy error of the set: proper morphism is translated as 完备态射 twice ("沿完备态射的前推", "完备 DM 叠"), i.e. 'complete' instead of 'proper', and perfect is also systematically rendered 完备 ("完备复形", "完备障碍理论"), collapsing two distinct hypotheses into one wrong word. It also deletes the entire commented-out figure block (~245 lines, including the commented explanation), though all live content is present, and drops 多 in 重覆盖 for multiple cover. Against that, the prose is among the most fluent and it helpfully glosses terms ("扭曲扇区（twisted sector）"); "equality of boundary divisors" is also mistranslated as 等价关系.

Complete and mathematically intact (formulas, labels and cites all preserved), but the weakest presentation: half-width ASCII punctuation (, : ( ) ?) is used throughout the Chinese prose, which is typographically wrong for academic Chinese. Terminology is poor and inconsistent: 引力下降部分 for gravitational descendants, 不动点轨迹 for fixed point set, 扭转扇形 for twisted sectors, 丛胚 for gerbe, and descendant/pluri-Hodge left untranslated. Fluency suffers from translationese ("利用 S_n 通过置换标记点而作用在…上的作用") and one verb-less broken sentence in the stem-invariant proposition ("它由公式 [align] 其中 N 表示…的法丛。").

A is complete and mathematically faithful, and its formulas, citations, and labels match the source exactly. The main weakness is terminology: “本征” for proper, “五次三维流形” for quintic threefold, and “开子栈” for open substack are less standard than “固有/紧合”, “五次三维簇”, and “开子叠”. It also leaves “fixed and ... is not a common zero” in English and uses colloquial phrasing such as “它活在”.

B is the most faithful and fluent overall, with every environment and formula present and strong terms such as “固有” and “局部完全交”. However, “特征” is used for a group character, and “并且对所有有理尾 C'，若 v = 0” leaves the quantifier for the preceding inequality awkwardly scoped. The two added small-font wrappers are minor LaTeX departures.

C preserves the full structure, but “(v_1, v_2) 不恒为零” weakens nonvanishing to “not identically zero”, a real hypothesis change. Presentation is also unpolished: the titles “Second toy example” and “Another toy example” remain in English, “Hassett's 的” doubles the possessive, and “fixed and ...” is untranslated. The mathematical LaTeX, labels, and environments are otherwise preserved exactly.

D preserves all formulas and environments and is generally faithful, with good choices such as “五次三维簇” and “格拉斯曼簇”. Its polish is uneven: “不是真的（proper）” reads as “not real”, the set condition remains in English as “fixed and ...”, and standalone “。” after displays is awkward. “不全为零” is also less precise than “处处非零” for the nonvanishing pair.

E is complete and generally faithful, but its terminology has several conspicuous errors: “旋子” means spinor rather than torsor, “特征” is used for character, and “壁与腔” or “GW 腔” is nonstandard for wall-and-chamber. “五次三维流形” and “一般满射” are also less precise than “五次三维簇” and “在一般点处满射”. The Chinese is otherwise fluent and the mathematical LaTeX is intact.

F changes “V is affine” to “V 是仿射空间”, strengthening the hypothesis from an affine object to affine space. It also renders perfect and proper as “完备”, prestable as “前稳定”, and weighted pointed as “加权标点”, while repeatedly adding or removing display punctuation and replacing the ét arrow label with “平展”. The prose is fluent and complete, but these mathematical and LaTeX departures are substantial.

G retains every environment and essentially all mathematical content, but “存在多于一个带长度 d_0 基点的次数 d_0” drops the noun for the tails and is mathematically incomplete. Terminology includes “虚循环” for virtual cycle and “腔” for chamber. Pervasive ASCII punctuation such as “曲线,这一问题” and “作用:”, together with standalone “。” after displays, makes the Chinese noticeably unpolished despite exact math and labels.

Complete and faithful: every environment, footnote, label, and formula is present and the tricky sentences (expected codimension, stability inequality, compact-type vertices) are all correct. Minor blemishes: 「全被压缩」 mistranslates 'all are contracted' (should be 收缩), and terminology leans Taiwan-style (「本征」 for proper, 「丰沛」 for ample) while 'nef' is left in English. The in-formula \text{ is bounded and nontrivial for all } is kept in English, matching the source. Fluent, natural academic Chinese overall.

Complete and generally faithful, but carries a cluster of small defects: 「当 \(X, V\) 时，上述猜想蕴含……」 is ungrammatical ('when (X,V)'), 「没有奇上同调」 reads as 'strange cohomology' rather than odd-degree cohomology, and 「全部被压缩」 mistranslates 'contracted'. Also adds words not in the source (「额外对数结构」, 「单个对数顶点」) and leaves 'nef' and 'étale' untranslated while translating 'ample'. LaTeX is pristine apart from an added \enlargethispage and inconsistent localization of cite pinpoints.

Byte-identical math and full completeness, but two renderings are genuinely confusing: 「态射 …… 非常好，但它不是真的」 renders 'it is not proper' as 'it is not true/real', and 「周围空间的全部自同构」 for 'ambient space' is nonstandard and inconsistent with the earlier 「环境（ambient）」. Other polish issues: 「一致界住」 for 'uniformly bounded', nef/orbifold/conifold gap left in English while ample is translated, and an uneven author-name translation policy. No mathematical claims are altered.

Excellent and complete, with standard consistent terminology (叠, 虚类, 一致极大退化, 余截面局部化) and all formulas, diagrams, labels, and cites preserved exactly. The one real error is shared with C: 「性质非常好，但它不是真的」 turns 'not proper' into 'not true', confusing since 真 is correctly used elsewhere (「是真且对数光滑的」). Otherwise only trivial inconsistencies (期望值/预期值, untranslated nef/étale/conifold) and mild translationese (「互相发送」).

Essentially flawless: complete to the last footnote and figure comment, with every formula and diagram byte-identical and no altered mathematical claims found on a full line-by-line read. Prose is genuinely natural (「性质很好，但不是紧合的」 handles 'very nice, but not proper' cleanly; 「考察它与 GW 理论相差多少」 is idiomatic). Only cosmetic blemishes: 预期/期望余维数 inconsistency, untranslated 'nef', and 零点集 for 'zero section' (arguably a sensible correction).

Complete and highly faithful with pristine LaTeX; no mistranslations or changed claims found, and all four unit-axiom items and the quintic computation are exact. Terminology is consistent but has debatable choices: 「专有」 for 'proper' ( mainland standard is 固有), 「锥流形」 for conifold, and 'nef' left in English while ample is translated. Occasional calques (「一个记住该零点的有理分量」, 「支在临界轨迹上」) keep fluency just below the top tier.

Accurate, complete, and LaTeX-perfect (it even translates the \text{...} inside the \L^{\circ} display correctly), but the entire file uses half-width ASCII punctuation in Chinese prose (「设 X 是一个光滑射影簇(甚至是 DM 叠)。…称为完全相交(complete intersection)。」), a pervasive typographic flaw. Other issues are minor: the recurring 「在期望余维数处光滑」 is misparsable as 'smooth at the expected codimension', and 「尖幺半群」, untranslated nef/orbifold, and 「一致地界住」 are nonstandard or colloquial.

All environments, equations, references, and both figures are retained, and the mathematical content is generally faithful. Terminology is occasionally inconsistent, using both “镜面” and “镜像” for mirror concepts, and the phrase “以前者由后者表出” is ungrammatical. One Picard–Fuchs display loses its final period, a minor LaTeX-fidelity issue.

All source environments and references are present, and the Chinese is the most fluent overall. There is one clear mathematical wording error: the space H is called a “辛变换” rather than a symplectic space (“辛空间”). Two displays are unnecessarily reformatted—the Yukawa-coupling row is split and the generator display is put in a gathered environment—so the LaTeX layout is not preserved exactly.

The translation is complete and preserves the mathematical LaTeX, labels, and citations exactly. However, “稳定相” is a nonstandard rendering of stationary phase (normally “驻相” or “稳相”), and “无脚” for graph legs is inconsistent with the earlier “腿”. Leaving basic display words such as “exists” and “for” in English also makes the final boundary-condition passage read less fully translated.

All equations and environments are present with clean LaTeX. The prose is faithful but more translationese-heavy, with “关联子” used alongside “关联函数”, “正规化” alongside “规范化”, and basic display words “exists” and “for” left in English. Phrases such as “在拼装二部其余图之后” are awkward, and “讲义写作之时” slightly shifts the meaning of “at the time of these lectures”.

The translation is complete and highly accurate, with consistent choices such as “轨形”, “锥形奇点”, and “虚拟闭链”, and natural academic Chinese overall. Minor weaknesses include “生成函数” for generating series and the nonstandard “壁穿越” for wall-crossing; “传播子的导数非常简单” also overtranslates “simply” as “very simple”. Four displays omit source-ending punctuation, but formulas, figures, labels, and citations are intact.

The unit is complete and the formulas are preserved, but the prose contains repeated avoidable English glosses and awkward terminology. Examples include “原生不变量” for primary invariants, “全纯模糊性” for holomorphic ambiguity, and especially “能级（level）” for a level of a tropical curve. “在一般意义下半单” weakens the mathematical meaning of “generically semisimple”, so this version needs more terminological revision than the higher-ranked ones.

All content is present, but key terminology is repeatedly wrong or inconsistent: “轨道点” and “轨道正则性” confuse orbifold with orbit, and “留数模式” is the wrong residue term in the mod-5 charge-rule passage. There are also visible prose errors such as “带理后代插入” and “完整的理后代插入” for rational descendant insertions. Eight displays drop source-ending punctuation, while labels, citations, equations, and figures otherwise remain intact.

The translation is faithful, fluent, and complete, with all equations and cross-references intact. However, “环 Calabi--Yau” and “环图” repeatedly drop 面 from 环面, and “已解消的锥形点” is not an adequate rendering of resolved conifold.

Generally accurate and readable, and the mathematical structure is fully preserved. The recurring “消解后的锥形奇点” misleadingly presents the resolved conifold as still singular, while “Lefschetz 膜” and “沿膜” are incorrect for Lefschetz thimble; the final sentence also repeats 对应 awkwardly.

All source content and LaTeX structures are present, but “不是真的” turns proper into real/true and loses the geometric claim about the moduli space. Phrases such as “扭理论” and the repeated typo “配为” (for 配对) make the Chinese less polished, although terms like “解消锥形” are handled well.

The prose is often elegant and the mathematics is complete, but “不是真（proper）的” is poor Chinese for proper and “Lefschetz 鞘” mistranslates thimble. “并认同” should be “并等同” in the identification of the basis vectors, and the added \bigskip is not in the source.

This is the smoothest and most consistent translation, with correct choices such as “紧合” for proper and “Lefschetz 顶针,” and with every formula and environment preserved. Its main defect is the recurring “消解锥形奇点” for resolved conifold, which wrongly retains a singularity; “三维流形” is also less precise than 三维簇 in this algebro-geometric context.

The translation is complete and preserves every equation exactly, but “不是专有的” renders proper as proprietary/exclusive, which is a clear mathematical mistranslation. Renderings such as “在一般意义下互不相同” for generically distinct and “整体定义的亚纯参考形式” are understandable but noticeably literal, so the academic Chinese is less natural.

The translation preserves the full argument and is generally readable, with sound choices such as “Lefschetz 顶针” and “固有” for proper. Nevertheless, “其作用保持 Calabi-Yau 型” confuses a differential form with a type, and “三维流形” plus the abbreviated “扭理论” weaken terminological precision; classifiers in “一个谱曲线” and “一个黎曼曲面” are also awkward.
summaries: All seven translations are complete and keep the abstract environment and \textbf, and all give the same names (周祐正, 方婷婷, 温耀雄, 郭帅). The main differences are how they handle the ambiguous parenthetical about which talks were live-TeXed, where B and F (and A) resolve it correctly and B does so most cleanly, and their register and punctuation. A is held back by half-width punctuation, and E and G by colloquial or redundant wording.

B is the strongest translation because it clearly separates the live-recording exceptions from later figure insertion and maintains fluent, faithful prose; A also preserves that distinction but needs small wording and punctuation edits. D, C, E, and G leave the exception's scope unclear, while F resolves it but introduces shifts concerning lecture errors and the notes supplied to Claude. All seven preserve the full abstract and its LaTeX structure, so the differences concern precision and style rather than missing material or broken markup.

All seven translations are complete and capture the overall meaning of the short abstract, with the main differentiator being how they handle the syntactic scope of the opening parenthetical ('live-TeXed (for all talks besides my own and those of Shuai Guo, some figures...)'). Translation B is the strongest because it cleanly resolves this parenthetical in natural academic Chinese without losing the logical scope, closely followed by D and C (which are fluent but leave the parenthetical scope ambiguous) and A (which is accurate on scope but uses half-width ASCII punctuation). F introduces a minor mistranslation ('以往' for 'other'), while E and G are overly colloquial and less natural.

All seven translations of the abstract are complete: every clause, the \textbf{experimental} emphasis, the three names, and the Codex/Claude Code remark are present in each. C and D track the English most closely and are the most publishable, while A and B are faithful with only punctuation or word-order issues and G follows close behind. E and F lose points for the nonstandard "试验性" and for the meaning shifts "讲义中的疏漏" and 课程 for "talks".

C is the standout: accurate scope, correct 实验性 for experimental, clean punctuation and preserved macros. D and G are also reliable, differing mainly in word choice (速记稿, 记录笔记) and dropped \TeX macros; A and E are faithful but stylistically rough (ASCII punctuation in A, 试验性 and translationese in E). B and F both misread the parenthetical so that live-TeXing appears to exclude the author's and Guo's talks, and F further calls the talks 课程 and softens errors to 疏漏.

C and D are the strongest: both fully accurate with clean, consistent Chinese, C marginally ahead since D's '现场 TeX 速记稿' is the only off-key term between them. E, G and A are all faithful, but E and G stumble over the same 'experimental AI-generated transcriptions' sentence while A is set throughout in half-width punctuation. The most fluent translation, B, and the weakest, F, both mis-scope the first sentence's exception, F additionally rendering 'errors' as '疏漏' and 'talks' as '课程'.

All seven translations of this short abstract are complete and broadly accurate, with the names, dates, and the \textbf{experimental} emphasis preserved. C stands out as publishable — faithful structure, academic register, clean punctuation and LaTeX — with D close behind. The rest cluster around 'good with minor issues': A loses points for half-width punctuation, B and F shift the meaning of the opening parenthetical by excluding the author's and Guo's talks from the live-TeXing itself, F also softens several terms (课程, 疏漏), and E and G slip into a colloquial register unsuited to an abstract.

All seven keep every environment, label, citation key and display intact, so the differences come from wording, terminology and leftover English. A is the cleanest and most natural throughout, spoiled mainly by English \text left in two displays, while E and B translate everything but have terminology inconsistencies or awkward constructions. C and D leave English optional arguments and display text, F and D add many English glosses (F with wrong terms such as 完备复形), and G mistypes Θ as θ in its headings.

All seven translations preserve the complete environment structure, diagrams, and displayed mathematical content; their differences are chiefly editorial and terminological. B and E are the most polished, with A close behind but retaining English text inside displays; D and C need more language editing, while F repeatedly mistranslates perfect complex. G is weakest because it changes the finite-presentation hypothesis, introduces inconsistent theta notation in headings, and contains conspicuous prose defects.

F is clearly the best translation, combining complete coverage (including math-embedded text) with natural Chinese syntax and clean LaTeX. E and G also translate all math-embedded text and read well, but E uses raw Unicode 'Θ' in section headings and '紧合的' for 'proper', while G erroneously replaces capital '\Theta' with lowercase '$\theta$' in three headings. B, D, A, and C lag behind due to awkward syntax (B, D), untranslated '\text{...}' or environment headers (A, C, D), and serious terminology flaws in A ('栈' for stack) and C ('无环的' for homological acyclicity).

All seven translations are complete (identical environment, item and equation counts) and none alters the mathematics; the differences lie in polish and terminology. B and E are the strongest, translating even the English text embedded in math mode into natural academic Chinese, while A and D are equally accurate but leave phrases like 'E is a vector bundle on C×T' and 'isomorphism classes in X(K)' inside their formulas (D additionally carries many English glosses). F, C and G trail on terminology and polish — F overloads 完备 for both 'perfect' and 'proper', C leaves several environment titles and 'Theorem 5.1' in English with a couple of typos, and G uses 过滤 for 'filtration', leaves many terms untranslated, and rewrites the section title with a lowercase \theta.

A and D are the best translations of this unit: accurate, complete, idiomatic and with math/labels preserved exactly (both minorly leave English \text fragments in displays and one '[informal]' label). C, E and B are all solid but each has distinct blemishes (C leaves three definition names in English, E uses nonstandard terms like 紧合 and 滤链, B has clumsy restructurings and a garbled formula caption), while F and G trail because of a systematic terminology error (F: 完备复形 for perfect complex, 完备 for proper) and markup inconsistencies (G: $\theta$ vs \Theta in headings, several typos). All seven cover every environment of the source without omissions.

All seven translations preserve the unit's structure — every definition, example, theorem, remark, exercise, the moduli-types table, all six tikzcd diagrams, the 64 display equations, labels and citation keys — so they differ mainly in terminology and polish. A, E, B and F are close to publishable, separated chiefly by single recurring lapses: '非交换' instead of '非阿贝尔' for non-abelian (A, B, E), '完备' doing double duty for proper/perfect (F), or a literal Unicode Θ in headings (E). C, D and G trail on standard terminology (proper as '真', pushforward as '推出函子', lowercase θ titles) and small accuracy slips in footnotes and quantifiers.

E is the strongest, combining complete, accurate mathematics with polished Chinese. A, B, and C are also thorough but lose polish through untranslated formula text or awkward phrasing; D, F, and G contain more noticeable terminology or editing errors, with F's “完备复形” and G's dropped “locally” especially important.

All seven keep every environment, equation, label, citation and the TikZ figure intact, so they differ on terminology and prose. E and A are near-publishable: E has the cleanest terminology (distinct '卡' for chart) and fully translated \text, and A is equally faithful. B reads best but uses '图' for chart. F, C, D and G each have a systematic term error: '上极限' for colimit, '对数积' for integral, and '有限' for fine; the last is the most damaging.

E and B are the strongest translations, with E combining especially consistent terminology, faithful hypotheses, and translated formula prose; A is accurate but more literal. C and F need targeted mathematical-language editing, while D has a recurring integral-terminology problem and G seriously confuses fine with finite. All seven retain the complete sequence of environments, equations, diagrams, and the figure, with labels and citation keys preserved.

Translation E is by far the strongest translation of Unit 02, combining complete mathematical accuracy, idiomatic Chinese mathematical prose, and consistent, well-chosen terminology (such as '卡' for chart and '相伴对数结构' for associated log structure). Translations B and A are solid and accurate but have minor terminology flaws ('伴随对数结构' and '图' for chart in B; '栈' for stack and untranslated equation text in A), while F is marred by a stray Japanese character ('图表の上极限'), CS terminology ('泛型点'), and editorial additions. Translations C, D, and G suffer from severe mathematical terminology errors: C and D mistranslate 'integral' as '对数积', and G mistranslates 'fine' as '有限的' (finite) throughout.

E, A and B are all publishable-quality: accurate, complete, with standard terminology, differing mainly in whether 'chart' and 'diagram' are kept distinct (A and E do; B uses bare 图) and in A's few untranslated inline conditions. C and F are usable but flawed — C conflates 图表 for chart and diagram and once renders 'integral' as 对数积, while F is weighed down by bilingual glosses, a stray Japanese の and 上极限/相切阶. D and G are held back by systematic term errors (D: integral → 对数积; G: fine → 有限的, plus 法相交 for normal crossings), which are the most serious meaning-changing defects in this unit.

All seven translations are complete and structurally faithful: every environment, equation, diagram and the tikz figure survive with matching labels and \cite keys, so the differences are mainly terminological and stylistic. A, E and B are publishable-quality, with A the most terminologically precise (proper 泛点/一般点 distinction) and only A leaving some \text{} fragments in English; F is close behind but padded with English glosses and marred by "上极限" for colimit and a stray の. C and D each stumble on "integral" (对数积, and "广义化" for generalization in C), while G is fluent but repeatedly mistranslates "fine" as "有限的" and "normal crossings" as "法相交", which misstates hypotheses and drops it to last place.

All seven translations are complete and preserve the LaTeX, labels, equations, tikzcd diagrams and the figure exactly, so they differ almost entirely on accuracy of terminology and quality of the Chinese. E and A are the best: accurate, consistent standard terminology and natural academic Chinese, with E additionally translating all text embedded in math. B is nearly as good but uses the confusing '图' for chart; C is solid apart from mistranslating 'integral' once as '对数积'. D and F suffer systematic terminology problems (D's '对数积' for integral in core definitions, F's '标点/泛型点/上极限' and a stray 'の'), while G is the weakest because 'fine' is rendered as '有限的', changing the mathematical claims themselves.

All seven translations are complete and structurally perfect (every environment, display, tikzcd diagram and the figure preserved, all labels and cite keys intact), so the differences are in accuracy and terminology. E is the cleanest and most fluent, with A, F and B close behind, each with minor blemishes (A leaves in-math \text in English and coins 鬼层; F has a の-for-的 typo and two small additions; B coins 伴随 and leaves étale/Cartesian untranslated). C, D and G suffer from terminology errors on core concepts: C has a one-off 对数积 plus a spurious 典范 and 广义化映射; D systematically coins 对数积 for integral and flip-flops between Chinese and bare English; G is the weakest, mistranslating "fine" as 有限的 throughout, which changes several mathematical claims.

All seven translations are structurally complete, with identical environments, labels and display math, so the differences are in accuracy details, terminology and style. A, B and E are close to publishable: A is the most faithful, B the most natural, and E is solid with a few non-standard terms. F reads well but has the tautological/典范 error and edits the display punctuation. G, D and C share a misreading of which object is toric, and D and C also switch inconsistently between Chinese transliterated and Western names, with C the most translationese.

All seven translations preserve the full unit, including every mathematical environment, both figures, and the long R-matrix computations. B and E offer the strongest combination of fidelity and readable Chinese; A, G, F, and D have localized terminology or interpretation problems, while C has the least fluent treatment of the oscillating-integral theorem. The differences are primarily in prose and technical vocabulary rather than omitted material or altered formulas.

Translation B is the strongest overall, combining accurate mathematical comprehension with natural Chinese phrasing and standard algebraic geometry terminology. Translations E and F are also fluent and accurate, but lose points for minor terminology flaws (E's '紧合的' for proper and '虚拟基本类'; F's '典范类/典范关系' for tautological class/relations). Among the remaining translations, G and A are serviceable despite A's use of '栈' for stack and '本征的' for proper, whereas D ('MSP 群') and especially C ('在各种前因子范围内', stiff translationese, and inconsistent transliterations) have more noticeable problems.

All seven translations are complete (every environment, figure, footnote and equation is present) and mathematically faithful; the differences are stylistic and terminological. E, A and B are the strongest, combining standard terminology with natural academic Chinese, with G and D close behind. F loses ground on '前稳定/典范类/谱系' plus equation-punctuation drift, while C is the most literal and contains the clear errors '真的' (proper) and '喉管' (thimble).

All seven translations of this unit are complete and structurally faithful: every theorem/example/definition/remark, both figures, all footnotes, labels and \cite keys survive, and the displayed mathematics is preserved essentially verbatim (E and C have byte-identical math apart from translated tikzcd labels). The ranking is decided by terminology and polish: E, D and A are publishable-quality with only isolated slips, while B, G, C and F each contain at least one real terminology error (膜 for thimble, 喉管, 典范类 for tautological) or an inconsistent naming policy. F is the weakest mainly because of the tautological/canonical mistranslation and its added glosses, despite fluent prose.

All seven translations of this unit are structurally complete: every definition, theorem, proof sketch, exercise, figure, label and citation survives, and the display mathematics is essentially intact throughout. The field separates on terminology and style: E, A and D are publishable with light copy-editing (E reads most naturally, A keeps the closest formal fidelity), B is solid but for a few recurring wrong word choices, and G, F and C are dragged down by repeated mistranslations — proper as 固有的/完备的/真的, universal as 泛, tautological as 典范 — of which C's '是真的' and garbled '在各种前因子范围内' are the most damaging single errors.

All seven translations are complete (every environment, figure, footnote, label and citation key preserved) and none is garbled, so the differences are in accuracy and terminology. G, B and E form the top tier: faithful, fluent, and terminologically sound, with G edging ahead by leaving the Chang-Guo-Li theorem header and tricky terms untouched rather than guessing. A, D and F are good but each has visible blemishes (untranslated "tautological" in A; "Lefschetz 闭链" and inconsistent term pairs in D; "完备的" for proper and math-punctuation drift in F). C is the weakest: still complete and compilable, but with genuine mistranslations ("在各种前因子范围内", "我" for "we", "是真的" for proper) and inconsistent transliterations.

All seven keep the math and labels intact, and all but B are complete. The main differences are how they render stratum, proper, crepant and torsor, and whether they leave English inside the math. A and E are the most faithful and consistent. C and D are close behind; both leave some English in the display. F and G suffer from mistranslated or mixed-language terms. B is the weakest because it moves the Verdier-duality clause into the perverse-sheaf definition and trims content.

D and E are the strongest overall, combining faithful mathematics with readable Chinese; A is similarly complete but more literal and less conventional in some terminology. B and C need localized editorial repairs, while G introduces a misleading singular-resolution phrase and confuses strata with stratifications. All seven preserve the main mathematical environments and displayed formulas; F ranks last because its translation of crepant adds an incorrect homological property.

Translations A, D, and F are the strongest overall: A and D combine high mathematical accuracy with solid terminology and clean LaTeX, while F has the most natural academic Chinese prose despite minor terminology flaws (such as "同调平凡解消" for crepant resolution). C, E, and G are very usable mid-tier translations held back by isolated terminology or accuracy errors (E's "W-旋子" for W-torsor, G's "奇异的 crepant 解消" for resolution of singularities, and C's untranslated math text). B ranks last primarily due to a severe LaTeX editing mistake that moved the end of a preceding sentence inside a "defn" environment.

All seven translations are complete: the environment counts, labels, footnotes, cite keys and every displayed equation match the English exactly, and the source's own quirks (the L_{|\lambda} typo) are reproduced everywhere. C and D are the strongest, combining accuracy with standard terminology (主齐性空间 / 真（proper）) and clean structure; E is a close third but for 'W-旋子'. A and F are faithful with terminology slips (本征映射; 同调平凡解消 and 可构层), G is clean but lexically weak (交同调), and B is the only translation with a structural defect, the displaced '满足 Verdier 对偶性。' now sitting inside the perverse-sheaf definition.

A is the clear winner: complete, accurate and idiomatic, with only cosmetic blemishes. D, B, E and C are all serviceable — B has the most standard terminology but a structural break at the Verdier duality sentence, D and E are fluent with occasional nonstandard terms (真/紧合, 旋子), and C is literal and calqued. F and G trail: F over-annotates and mistranslates crepant and proper, while G leaves theorem names in English and mistranslates 'resolution of singularities'.

All seven translations are structurally complete — identical environment counts, all equations, footnotes and \cite keys — and none changes the mathematics in the displayed formulas; they separate on terminology and polish. A is the most publishable overall; E, C and D follow closely, where E fully translates the math-text fragments but uses coined terms, while C and D keep the cleanest standard vocabulary but leave two displayed fragments in English. B, G and F trail for concrete reasons: a displaced sentence typeset inside a definition box (B), one genuine mistranslation plus English leftovers in running text (G), and systematically wrong renderings of 'proper' and 'hard Lefschetz' (F).

A is the strongest overall, with C and D close behind but needing terminology and polish; B is fluent but loses ground through a misplaced Verdier-duality clause and an incomplete phrase in the final equation. G and E are usable with more terminology problems, while F is the weakest because ‘完备’ and ‘同调平凡解消’ alter important mathematical concepts.

All seven keep the math, labels, citations and figures essentially intact, so the differences come down to terminology and prose. E and B read most like real Chinese mathematical writing. E is slightly more faithful, while B has small meaning shifts and LaTeX tweaks. A, C and D are solid but each has a repeated term problem or translationese (推出 for pushforward, terms left in English, 惰性叠). F conflates proper and perfect as 完备. G is let down by ASCII punctuation throughout, garbled sentences and several wrong terms.

B and E are the strongest overall, combining complete mathematical coverage with the most readable Chinese; C and D preserve the content well but need more sentence-level editing. A has conspicuous terminology problems around proper pushforward, F conflates properness with perfectness, and G has the weakest technical phrasing and fluency. All seven preserve every active environment, equation, and figure, with identical active TikZ code and intact labels and citation keys; F's shorter length mainly reflects removal of commented-out material.

All seven translations preserve the full mathematical content, environments, and figures of Unit 05, with Translation E standing out for its natural Chinese prose, consistent terminology, and clean handling of sentences containing displayed equations. Translations B and C are solid runners-up with good terminology but minor formatting or word-order issues around displayed math, whereas A and D suffer from non-standard terminology ('栈', '推出') or incomplete clauses and orphan punctuation. Translations F and G rank lowest: F conflates 'proper' and 'perfect' by translating both as '完备', while G uses half-width ASCII punctuation throughout Chinese text, mistranslates 'gravitational descendants' as '引力下降部分', and leaves broken sentences around equations.

All seven translations are essentially complete and preserve the mathematics (display equations are identical everywhere; only added sentence-final periods and minor equation ordering differ). B, E and A are the strongest: standard terminology (固有/紧合态射, 伪不变量), clean full-width punctuation and faithful handling of every environment and the tikz figures. C and D are solid but slightly less polished (leftover English 'fake/stem', nonstandard '惰性叠', ASCII straight quotes), while F and G fall behind on terminology — F conflates proper and perfect under '完备', and G uses only half-width punctuation plus invented terms such as '丛胚' and '引力下降部分'.

All seven translations of this unit are complete — every environment, equation, footnote and both active figures survive in each (F's apparent gaps are only the source's dead commented-out block), and the TikZ diagrams and math are byte-identical to the English. A is the standout: accurate, fluent and carefully terminological, while B and C are close behind with only typographic or spacing blemishes; D and E each wobble on a few standard terms (惰性叠, 紧合态射). F and G rank last for opposite reasons — F is fluent but mistranslates perfect/proper as 完备 throughout and misnames the KdV hierarchy, whereas G is accurate but writes all Chinese punctuation in halfwidth form and mishandles a handful of terms.

All seven translations of unit 05 are complete and mathematically faithful: every display equation, environment, citation key and both figures match the source in each, so the differences lie almost entirely in Chinese style. B and E are the most polished, with standard consistently-used terminology and natural prose; A is nearly as good but makes odder choices ('本征态射', '胀子方程'); C and D are solid with scattered inconsistencies; F is the most fluent but systematically renders both perfect and proper as '完备' and drops a commented-out figure block; G is accurate but set with half-width commas throughout.

All seven translations of unit 05 are complete in their live content and preserve the math, labels and citations essentially verbatim, so the ranking is decided by terminology precision, fluency and small LaTeX defects. E and A form the top tier — accurate, complete and natural, with only mild terminological quirks (E's 紧合态射, A's 推出 for pushforward) — followed by B and C, which are strong but marred by isolated mistranslations (B's 孤立的有理曲线 for 'unique') or inconsistent terminology policy (C's untranslated orbifold/fake/stem and coined 多霍奇). D, F and G trail: F commits the only hypothesis-changing error (proper→完备) and deletes the commented-out figure block, D has 惰性叠 plus reordered displays and quote bugs, and G combines weak terminology with pervasive half-width punctuation.
